problem: Most social navigation systems use fixed personal/group space parameters, or adapt only for human avoidance in static scenes, so a robot cannot closely approach individuals or groups (especially moving ones) for interaction while respecting comfort.
motivation: Robots in human environments need to proactively initiate interaction, which requires getting closer than the edge of standard personal/group space without breaching intimate space. Space models must therefore adapt to group arrangement, human velocity and the robot's own size.
key_idea: Adapt Gaussian personal/group space parameters (front, lateral, velocity-dependent) and the approach-pose search (FOV filtering, robot-fit check, velocity-scaled expansion) inside ROS costmap_2d/move_base so a robot can safely get close to static or moving humans and groups.
insight: Adaptation only helps when the group geometry leaves real free space: gains were largest for 3-person groups (+15% approach perimeter) and smaller for 2-person groups, or when the robot was larger (5.4% vs 10.7% on IDIAP). In dynamic simulation, adapting the space model alone was nonfunctional, and only combining space-model and approach-pose velocity adaptation was consistent. In the real-robot test, the adaptive algorithm cut the final distance from 1.265 to 1.052 m.
method: Altered Asymmetric Gaussian: extends the Kirby 2D asymmetric Gaussian to four independent standard deviations (front, rear, left, right); personal spaces are merged with max, plus a group-space Gaussian
Individual adaptation: lowers the frontal sigma by a preset zeta (0.3 m), floored at Hall's intimate space (0.45 m)

Group adaptation: computes lateral auxiliary points of neighbouring members, checks whether the gap fits the robot width s_r, and shrinks lateral sigmas (floored at 0.225 m) to open an approach corridor
Velocity adaptation: frontal sigma is increased in proportion to human/group speed (a_adapt, a_limit), scaled down by distance to the robot (d_limit)

Approach pose estimation: filters the approach circle by the common field of view of all members and by whether the zone fits the robot, then picks the closest valid pose; for moving targets it enlarges the max radius, the expansion step and narrows the FOV with radius
ROS integration: custom costmap_2d Adaptive Layer and Clean People Layer with move_base; OpenPose + homography for human pose, hierarchical clustering for groups
Evaluation: Human Safety and Comfort Indexes (SII, SGI, SDI) with threshold 0.14

setting.backbone: Hand-crafted geometric algorithms (Gaussian cost layers, approach pose search) with ROS move_base; OpenPose for human detection
setting.observation: RGB camera (OpenPose 2D pose + homography to 3D), laser/costmap for obstacles
setting.action_space: Goal poses to ROS move_base (velocity commands from local planner)
setting.simulator: Gazebo 9 (ROS Melodic) with the Vizzy robot, plus real-world Vizzy
setting.privileged: none for the real robot; in simulation the human models' poses are presumably known

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; results are dataset perimeter increases, HSCI plots, and real-robot distance statistics (not in canonical benchmark format).
results: On the IDIAP Poster dataset the adaptation increases the approach perimeter by up to 10.7% (human-sized robot, s_h=0.225 m; Vizzy-sized 5.4%) and on Synthetic data by 5% and 3.6% over Melo's algorithm. In the real robot test, the final distance dropped from 1.265 m (σ=0.0470) to 1.052 m (σ=0.0295) (p=7.98e-10), and 52.6% of participants preferred the new algorithm vs 15.8% preferring the original, though only 'Awkward' was significant in the Godspeed questionnaire.
limitations: Cannot handle human-object interactions and cannot rank valid approach poses
Velocity adaptation is simplistic (linear motion only), and costmap updates are under-optimized and can be too slow for real dynamic scenes
Dynamic experiments only in simulation; real-life tests are small (19 volunteers; the distance test used a single participant, the author) and mostly non-significant
compares_to: Melo's adaptive space and approach pose algorithm (non-adaptive version)
